finding.smtp_security.auth_cleartext: PLAIN or LOGIN authentication advertised before any encryption on {hosts}
finding.smtp_security.banner_version: The banner of {host} discloses the software and its version ({software} {version})
finding.smtp_security.catch_all: The server accepts any recipient of the domain (catch-all): spam and made-up addresses arrive unfiltered
finding.smtp_security.cert_untrusted: Untrusted TLS certificate on {hosts} (self-signed, unknown chain or name differing from the MX)
finding.smtp_security.no_starttls: STARTTLS not offered by {hosts}: inbound mail travels in cleartext
finding.smtp_security.open_relay: Open relay suspected on {hosts}: the server accepts an external recipient from an external sender (to be confirmed)
finding.smtp_security.tls_failed: STARTTLS advertised but TLS negotiation fails on {hosts}
module.smtp_security.checks: Connects to the MX servers (port 25): banner and software, STARTTLS, TLS version and certificate, AUTH methods advertised in cleartext, catch-all domain. The open relay test is optional and disabled by default. No message is ever sent.
module.smtp_security.fix:
Suspected open relay (handle first): close it right away. Let only trusted networks and authenticated users relay (on Postfix: `smtpd_relay_restrictions` ending with `defer_unauth_destination`, and `mynetworks` limited to your own addresses, never an Internet range). Then review the mail queue and the logs for abusive sending.
Mail hosted by a provider (Microsoft 365, Google Workspace, shared hosting): TLS, certificate and banner are theirs to manage; open a ticket with the finding, and check that no MX points to a forgotten internal server.
STARTTLS missing or negotiation failing: enable TLS on port 25 of the mail server with a valid certificate, for example on Postfix `smtpd_tls_security_level = may` with `smtpd_tls_cert_file` and `smtpd_tls_key_file` (`smtpd_tls_protocols = >=TLSv1.2` needs Postfix 3.6 or later), then reload the service.
Expired or untrusted certificate: issue a trusted certificate (for example Let's Encrypt) whose name is EXACTLY the MX name, with the full chain, renewed automatically, then reload the service.
PLAIN or LOGIN authentication offered before TLS: offer AUTH only after STARTTLS (on Postfix `smtpd_tls_auth_only = yes`) and send users to port 587 (STARTTLS) or 465 (implicit TLS) for submission. If passwords may have travelled in cleartext, change them.
Banner that discloses the software and its version: shorten the text (on Postfix `smtpd_banner = $myhostname ESMTP`) and above all update the software; hiding the version is only a complement.
Catch-all (the server accepts any recipient): if it is not intended, turn it off in the admin console so nonexistent addresses are refused during the SMTP dialogue; if it is intended, filter spam and monitor the mailbox.
Check with `openssl s_client -starttls smtp -connect mx1.example.com:25 -servername mx1.example.com` (the result must show a successful verification: `Verify return code: 0 (ok)` or `Verification: OK`), then run the scan again.
module.smtp_security.fix_snippet:
# Postfix main.cf
smtpd_tls_security_level = may
smtpd_tls_cert_file = /etc/ssl/certs/mx1.example.com-fullchain.pem
smtpd_tls_key_file = /etc/ssl/private/mx1.example.com.key
smtpd_tls_protocols = >=TLSv1.2
smtpd_tls_auth_only = yes
smtpd_relay_restrictions = permit_mynetworks, permit_sasl_authenticated, defer_unauth_destination
smtpd_banner = $myhostname ESMTP
# Postfix CLI
postconf mynetworks smtpd_relay_restrictions
postfix reload
# openssl
openssl s_client -starttls smtp -connect mx1.example.com:25 -servername mx1.example.com
module.smtp_security.title: SMTP probe
module.smtp_security.why: A mail server without STARTTLS exposes inbound mail to eavesdropping, cleartext authentication exposes passwords, and an open relay lets attackers send spam through the server.
smtp_security.err_banner_refused: the server refuses the connection at the banner (scanner address probably blocked)
smtp_security.err_blocked: address refused by the target policy
smtp_security.no_mx: The domain publishes no MX record
smtp_security.no_server_examined: None of the {count} MX server(s) could be examined (banner refused or dialogue interrupted)
smtp_security.null_mx: The domain declares it accepts no mail (null MX, RFC 7505)
smtp_security.port_filtered: None of the {count} MX server(s) is reachable on port 25 (often blocked by the ISP, cloud provider or local firewall); submission (587) was tried without success
smtp_security.score_ok: STARTTLS with a valid certificate, no cleartext authentication
